messages.text:
Ivo proposes **$42,500 for a guaranteed block of 50 design days**. That’s $850 per day against Ivo’s usual $900 rate. Ivo would reserve the block once both parties sign and Hearth pays a 30% deposit of $12,750 within three business days of signing. The next 40% ($17,000) would be due on delivery of the developed design, and the final 30% ($12,750) on delivery of the fabrication-ready design package.

The fee covers concept design, developed design, fabrication drawings, and two rounds of revisions based on consolidated museum feedback. We propose one round after concept review and one after developed-design review. Hearth and Ivo would agree on accessibility requirements, touring constraints, and deliverables at signing.

Hearth would have permission to fabricate, exhibit, and tour the agreed design. Ivo would have permission to show cleared photographs in their portfolio and presentations after the public opening, with museum and photographer credits. Fabrication supervision would be booked separately at $900 per day on dates agreed in advance.

What is the fabricator’s drawing deadline, and can Hearth release the deposit within three business days? If the deposit timetable is fixed by procurement, Ivo is open to discussing a smaller guaranteed block at the standard rate.

Hearth proposes **$41,400 for 46 guaranteed days at Ivo’s standard $900 rate**. The block includes 44 design days and two on-site installation days. Hearth can release a **20% deposit of $8,280 within three business days of signing**. We propose three further payments, each due within ten business days of delivery or completion.

| Milestone | Payment |
|---|---:|
| Concept package | $8,280 |
| Developed design | $12,420 |
| Fabrication-ready package, including editable files, and completion of both installation days | $12,420 |

The scope includes concept design, developed design, fabrication drawings, and an accessible alternate layout detailed for fabrication. We accept one consolidated revision round after concept review and one after developed-design review. At signing, we’d attach a brief covering access requirements, venue constraints, and file formats the fabricator can use. Any further site supervision would require a separate written booking.

Ivo would retain copyright. Hearth requests a perpetual, nonexclusive license to use and edit the files to fabricate, install, exhibit, maintain, and adapt this exhibit across touring venues. Hearth could share the files with its fabricators and host venues for those purposes. Ivo could use cleared photographs in portfolios and presentations **after the touring venue opens**, currently expected two months after launch. Hearth would confirm the opening and photo clearance in writing, with museum and photographer credits.

The fabricator’s drawing deadline is still unconfirmed. Hearth proposes fixing the concept review, developed-design review, drawing delivery, and two installation dates in the agreement before signature. **Can Ivo accept the 46-day block on these terms and give us the minimum lead time needed from deposit to drawing delivery, including time for museum feedback?** That will let Hearth test the schedule with the fabricator before the slot expires.

Ivo can commit to **46 guaranteed days for $41,400**, with 44 design days and two installation days on dates fixed before signature. The minimum lead time from deposit to fabrication-ready drawings is **50 business days**, assuming Ivo has the agreed brief, venue drawings, and exhibit content when the deposit arrives. The schedule allows 44 working days and two museum review periods of three business days each. Hearth would provide one consolidated response per review. Feedback or inputs received late would move drawing delivery by the corresponding delay.

Ivo accepts the $8,280 deposit within three business days of signing, $8,280 on concept delivery, and $12,420 on developed-design delivery. Ivo proposes splitting the last $12,420 into **$10,620 on delivery of the fabrication-ready package** and **$900 on completion of each installation day**. Each post-deposit payment would be due within ten business days of its milestone.

The drawing package would include the accessible alternate layout and editable files in the agreed formats. Ivo accepts Hearth’s proposed touring license, including edits and file sharing for the stated exhibit purposes, with Ivo retaining copyright. Fabrication supervision beyond the two scheduled installation days would require a separate written booking with dates agreed in advance.

Ivo asks to use cleared photographs of the launch installation in portfolios and presentations **from the exhibit’s first public opening**. Images specific to a later venue could be shown once that venue opens. Hearth would confirm clearance and the required credits in writing.

Can the fabricator accommodate the 50-business-day window, and can Hearth agree to the payment split and venue-specific photo timing?

Hearth accepts the **50-business-day lead time** from receipt of the deposit, agreed brief, venue drawings, and exhibit content. We can commit to one consolidated response within three business days at each review and accept a corresponding extension for late inputs or feedback. We still need the fabricator to confirm its drawing deadline before we can say the slot works. Before signature, we’ll record the two review dates, drawing deadline, and both installation dates in the agreement.

Hearth can move the **$10,620 drawing payment** forward if we combine the installation fees into one **$1,800 payment after the second installation day**. That keeps the $41,400 guarantee and fits our limit of three payments after the deposit.

| Payment trigger | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Signature | $8,280 |
| Delivery of developed design | $20,700 |
| Delivery of fabrication-ready package | $10,620 |
| Completion of second installation day | $1,800 |

The deposit is due within three business days of signing. Each milestone payment is due within ten business days. Concept delivery and its review remain on the schedule. If payment at concept delivery is important to Ivo, Hearth can keep the earlier schedule of $8,280 at concept, $12,420 at developed design, and $12,420 after drawing delivery and both installation days.

The sponsor’s embargo covers **all exhibit photographs, including launch photographs, until the touring venue opens**, currently expected two months after launch. Once it opens, Ivo may use cleared photographs in portfolios and presentations with the credits Hearth confirms in writing.

Which payment schedule works for Ivo, and can Ivo agree to that photo release date? The scope, editable files, accessible alternate layout, and touring license are agreed.

Ivo accepts the schedule with **$8,280 due within three business days of signing**, $20,700 on developed-design delivery, $10,620 on delivery of the fabrication-ready package, and $1,800 after the second installation day. Each post-deposit payment is due within ten business days of its milestone. Concept delivery and review remain on the agreed schedule.

Ivo also accepts the embargo on all exhibit photographs until the touring venue opens. After that opening, Ivo may use cleared photographs in portfolios and presentations with the credits Hearth confirms in writing.

Once the fabricator confirms a drawing deadline that accommodates the agreed 50-business-day window, please send the agreement for signature with the brief, both review dates, the drawing deadline, and both installation dates attached.

Hearth proposes scheduling Ivo’s two on-site days around two distinct checks.

- **Installation day.** Ivo, the local installer, and Hearth’s access lead would walk through the installed exhibit against the accessibility requirements in the brief. We’d schedule the walk-through early enough for the installer to make corrections during their one available day. Ivo and Hearth would record any open items and who will address them.
- **Opening day.** Before visitors enter, Ivo and Hearth’s access lead would repeat the checks in the final layout and co-sign a dated test report recording the results, any outstanding issues, and who will address them. Hearth would arrange any physical corrections needed after the installer’s day.

The sponsor releases its second payment to Hearth against the signed report. For Ivo’s fee, Hearth proposes that the **final $1,800 be due within ten business days of delivery of the co-signed opening-day report**, regardless of when the sponsor pays Hearth. The $41,400 fee and the first three payments stay as agreed. Hearth would attach the checklist, report template, and both attendance dates to the agreement before signature.

Can Ivo reserve opening day as the second on-site day and agree to the joint checks and revised final payment trigger?

The three-week shift puts both revised dates in conflict with an existing commission. Ivo can provide a local installation assistant for both on-site checks and join **one live remote signoff before visitors enter on opening day**.

On installation day, the assistant would walk the exhibit with Hearth’s access lead early enough for the installer to make corrections. They would record measurements, checklist results, and an owner for each open item. On opening day, the assistant and access lead would repeat the checks in the final layout. Ivo would join by video to review the results and any outstanding issues. The report would identify who performed the physical checks and what Ivo verified remotely. Ivo and Hearth’s access lead would co-sign it that day.

Ivo proposes keeping the **$41,400 fee**, including the assistant’s attendance and Ivo’s remote signoff. The first three payments would stay as agreed. Ivo accepts the final **$1,800 due within ten business days of delivery of the co-signed report**, regardless of sponsor payment.

Can Hearth confirm that the sponsor accepts this form of signoff and send the revised dates and pre-opening time for booking? The agreement can then name the assistant and attach the checklist and report template reflecting those roles.

Hearth can accept the proposed staffing at **$41,400**, subject to written sponsor approval. We’ll ask the sponsor to confirm that it will release its second payment against a report that identifies the assistant and Hearth’s access lead as the on-site testers and Ivo as the designer who reviewed the results live by video.

On installation day, the assistant and Hearth’s access lead would run the checklist early enough for the local installer to make corrections that day. On opening day, the assistant and access lead would repeat the checks before visitors enter. Ivo would join once by video to review the findings, then co-sign the report with the access lead that day. Hearth would handle any physical corrections after installation day.

The final **$1,800 would be due within ten business days of delivery of the co-signed report**, regardless of when the sponsor pays Hearth. The first three payments remain as agreed.

Please send the assistant’s name and a brief summary of their experience checking exhibit accessibility so we can include them in the sponsor request. Sponsor acceptance, the revised dates, and the pre-opening time are still unconfirmed. Hearth will send the confirmed dates and local time for booking and attach the agreed checklist and report template before signature.

The assistant’s name and accessibility-check experience are still to be confirmed. Please send the provisional dates, venue, pre-opening time window, and draft checklist when available. Ivo can use those details to verify the assistant’s availability and relevant experience, then provide their name and a brief summary for the sponsor.

In the meantime, can Hearth ask the sponsor to review the proposed signoff arrangement in principle, with the named assistant subject to written approval? Ivo’s booking remains subject to that approval and confirmation of the dates and local time.

Yes. Hearth will ask the sponsor to review the signoff arrangement in principle now, with written approval of the named assistant to follow. We’ll ask whether the sponsor will release its second payment against a report that identifies who performed the physical checks and what Ivo verified by video, co-signed on opening day by Ivo and Hearth’s access lead.

The provisional dates, venue, and pre-opening window are still pending. We’ll send those details, including the local time zone, as soon as they’re available. Ivo can then confirm the assistant’s availability and provide their name and relevant experience for approval.

**Draft checklist for review**

- **Installation day.** The assistant and Hearth’s access lead measure the accessible route, clearances, and reach heights against the agreed brief and drawings. They check access to labels, controls, and alternate exhibit content. They record results, flag corrections for the installer during their one available day, and assign an owner to each open item.
- **Opening day, before visitors enter.** The assistant and access lead repeat the checks in the final layout and record which corrections they verified. Ivo joins one live video session to review the measurements, results, and outstanding items. The report names the on-site testers, identifies the evidence Ivo reviewed remotely, and records any further action. Ivo and the access lead co-sign it that day.

Booking remains subject to written sponsor approval of the arrangement and assistant, and confirmation of both dates and the local signoff time. The final **$1,800 is due within ten business days of delivery of the co-signed report**, regardless of when Hearth receives sponsor funds.

Ivo accepts the draft checklist for inclusion in the sponsor request and agreement. The report should record the measured values alongside the requirements in the brief so Ivo can review them during the live session. Ivo’s signature will confirm the evidence reviewed and the findings recorded, including any items still open.

Once Hearth provides the venue, both dates, and the local pre-opening window, Ivo can confirm availability and submit the assistant’s name and relevant experience for written sponsor approval.

Agreed. Hearth will include the checklist and report template in the sponsor request and agreement. The report will show each measured value beside the corresponding requirement in the brief. It will identify the on-site testers and record the evidence Ivo reviewed live, the findings, and any open items. Ivo’s signature will confirm that review and those findings.

Hearth will seek the sponsor’s in-principle approval and send the venue, both dates, and the local pre-opening window as soon as they’re available. Booking remains pending until the schedule is confirmed and the sponsor approves the arrangement and named assistant in writing.
